questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The pH of 1 N aqueous solutions of HCl , $\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{COOH}$ and HCOOH follows the order:
questions.solution:
Stronger the acid, lower is the pH or weaker the acid, higher the pH.
The strength of the given acid is in the order
$\mathrm{HCl}>\mathrm{HCOOH}>\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{COOH}$
Hence, their pH is in the order
$\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{COOH}>\mathrm{HCOOH}>\mathrm{HCl}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: 20 mL of 0.1 M acetic acid is mixed with 50 mL of potassium acetate. $K_\alpha$ of acetic acid $=1.8 \times 10^{-5}$ at $27^{{}^{\circ}} \mathrm{C}$. Calculate the concentration of potassium acetate if pH of mixture is 4.8.
questions.solution:
For an acidic buffer,
$\mathrm{pH}=\mathrm{p} K_\alpha+\log \frac{[\text{ Salt }]}{[\text{ Acid }]}\ldots(i)$
Let the concentration of potassium acetate solution $=x \mathrm{M}$ 20 mL of 0.1 M acetic acid $=20 \times 0.1 \mathrm{millimol}=2$ millimol
50 mL of $x \mathrm{M}$ potassium acetate $=x \times 50 \mathrm{millimol}\begin{aligned}
& =50 x \text{ milimol } \\
\mathrm{pH} & =4.8
(Given)\end{aligned}$
Substitute all value in eq. (i),
$\begin{aligned}
4.8 & =-\left(\log 1.8+10^{-5}\right)+\log \frac{50 x}{2} \\
\log 25 x & =0.06 \\
x & =0.04 \mathrm{M}
\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: $pH$ of a saturated solution of $Ba\left(OH\right)^{2}$ is $12$. The value of its ${K}_{sp}$ is
questions.solution:
Given that,

pH of $Ba\left(OH\right)^{2} = 12$

$∵ pH + pOH = 14$

$∴ pOH = 14 - pH = 14 - 12 = 2$

Now, $pOH = - \log \left[{OH}^{-}\right]$

$⇒ 2 = - \log \left[OH\right]

\left[{OH}^{-}\right] =${10}^{- 2}M$

\mathop{Ba\left(OH\$\right)^{2}$\left(s\right)_{{SmolL}^{- 1}} ⇌ \mathop{Ba2 +}_{S} + \mathop{2{OH}^{-}}_{2S}$

$\left[{OH}^{-}\right]$ =$2S = {10}^{- 2}M$

$∴ S = 0. 5 $\times {10}^{- 2} =$5 $\times {10}^{- 3}$ M$

${K}_{sp} = \left[{Ba}^{2 +}\right]\left[{OH}^{-}\right]2$

$⇒ ( 5 \times {10}^{- 3} ) {( {10}^{- 2} )}^{2} =5 \times {10}^{- 7}M^{3}$

Therefore, the value of ${K}_{sp}$ is $5. 0 \times {10}^{- 7}M^{3}$.

$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: ${BF}_{3}$ is an acid, according to
questions.solution:
${BF}_{3}$ is a Lewis acid, as it accepts lone pair of electrons.

It is not an Arrhenius acid because it does not furnish $H^{+}$ ion in its aqueous solution.

It is also not a Bronsted Lowry acid as if does not give $H^{+}$& ions in any solvent.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the correct increasing order of Bronsted bases?
questions.solution: $\mathrm{ClO}_{4}^{-}< \mathrm{ClO}_{3}^{-}< \mathrm{ClO}_{2}^{-}< \mathrm{ClO}^{-}$ is the correct increasing order of Bronsted base. With increase in the number of oxygen atoms in the conjugate bases, the delocalisation of the $\pi$ bond becomes more and more extended. This results in decrease in the electron density. Consequently basicity also decreases.

$\mathrm{CO}_{2}+\mathrm{H}_{2} \mathrm{O} \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{H}_{2} \mathrm{CO}_{3} \rightarrow \mathrmH^{+}+\mathrm{HCO}_{3}^{-}$
